The position after Ke6 Nc5+ Kf7 already wins because h8=Q is unstoppable. So **Ke6** is the winning move! It attacks the undefended knight, and after either Nf8+ or Nc5+, White either captures it on f8 with check or pushes the h-pawn to victory after Kf7.

**Coaching Note:**

The knight on d7 was Black's only defender against your advancing pawns. By playing Ke6, you attacked it and forced it to give check while moving away. On f8, it's captured with check; on c5, your king simply walks toward promotion. The key lesson: **Identify the defender and attack it. Sometimes the strongest move isn't forcing an immediate capture, but removing the key piece that stops your plan.**
